name: Fr. Francisco de Paula Sanchez, S.J.

role.en: Jesuit priest and Rizal's Ateneo teacher; his fellow surveyor in Dapitan
role.fil: Paring Heswita at guro ni Rizal sa Ateneo; kasama niya sa pagsukat ng lupain sa Dapitan
role.de: Jesuitenpater und Rizals Lehrer am Ateneo; sein Mitstreiter bei den Vermessungen in Dapitan

portrait.alt: Framed photograph of Fr. Francisco de Paula Sanchez seated in biretta and cassock before a painted backdrop
portrait.credit: Herbosa Collection of the Rizal Library, Ateneo de Manila University

author: Jane Maren Dasal

quote.en: Our professor was a model of correctness, enthusiasm, and zeal for the advancement of his pupils. So great was his zeal that I, who hardly spoke passable Spanish, in a short time succeeded in writing fairly good compositions. His name is Francisco de Paula Sanchez.
quote.fil: Ang aming propesor ay huwaran ng kawastuhan, sigasig, at pananabik para sa pagsulong ng kanyang mga mag-aaral. Napakatindi ng kanyang sigasig anupat ako, na halos hindi makapagsalita ng katanggap-tanggap na Espanyol, sa maikling panahon ay nagtagumpay na makasulat ng medyo mahuhusay na komposisyon. Ang kanyang pangalan ay Francisco de Paula Sanchez.
quote.de: Unser Professor war ein Vorbild an Genauigkeit, Begeisterung und Eifer für den Fortschritt seiner Schüler. So groß war sein Eifer, dass ich, der ich kaum passables Spanisch sprach, in kurzer Zeit recht gute Aufsätze zu schreiben vermochte. Sein Name ist Francisco de Paula Sanchez.

bio.en:
Aside from his family, only a few were privileged to witness Dr. Rizal's genius in his youth and until his adulthood and martyrdom. Father Francisco de Paula Sanchez, a Jesuit priest, was one such person.

Born on 12 January 1849 in Tarragona, Spain, Fr. Sanchez entered the seminary of Tortosa at the age of 13 and later became a novice of the Jesuit order. He eventually took his vows after some years, when he was 18. His passion for literature was solidified in Balaguer, Spain and Avignon, France where he finished his literary studies. He also became well-versed in rhetoric, philosophy, and Latin.

Fr. Sanchez and Rizal crossed paths at the Ateneo Municipal de Manila. He had just arrived in the Philippines on 31 October 1872, taught at the school, and became Rizal's teacher from 1874 to 1875. Rizal, by this time, was already in his fourth year at Ateneo Municipal.

Fr. Sanchez was highly regarded by Rizal, who learned mathematics, rhetoric, Greek, and Spanish from the Jesuit. When Rizal entered his class, the boy's Spanish was subpar, but he advanced quickly in speaking and using the language in poetry. Fr. Sanchez assigned the young “Pepito” to adapt the Italian drama St. Eustachius, Martyr, written in Spanish prose, into verse. Rizal's fondness for his teacher was written in the introduction of his work on St. Eustachius, where he called him “my beloved professor” and expressed his gratitude for his efforts to help him in his studies.

He also trained Rizal further in poetry. The training back then was proposing a subject, either historical or religious, and expanding the themes through poems. One of his other assignments for Rizal was to write a poem about Calamba, his hometown.

Despite Rizal's praise of his teaching style, Fr. Sanchez was seen as pessimistic and enigmatic by other students. Fr. Sanchez later returned to Europe, spending time in Italy, France, and Spain to study. He was ordained as a priest in 1880, then returned to the Philippines as a teacher at the Ateneo Municipal in 1881.

Over the years, Rizal and Fr. Sanchez remained in contact. He praised the Noli Me Tangere but also warned the novelist about the dangers because of the novel's contents. Fr. Sanchez would circle back to the orbit of Rizal's life when he was recommended by Fr. Pastells to also be sent to Dapitan during Rizal's exile there, “to see if this strayed sheep can be brought to the right path”, referring to Rizal's anti-cleric views. The two also ventured into scientific endeavors in Dapitan: sharing scientific equipment, conducting archaeological excavations, and making a relief map of Mindanao. Fr. Sanchez left Dapitan in 1883 when he was reassigned to Tagana-an, Surigao. He outlived his prized student Rizal by 32 years, dying from a stomach illness on 21 July 1928.
bio.fil:
Bukod sa kanyang pamilya, iilan lamang ang nagkaroon ng pribilehiyong masaksihan ang henyo ni Dr. Rizal sa kanyang kabataan hanggang sa kanyang pagtanda at pagkamartir. Si Padre Francisco de Paula Sanchez, isang paring Heswita, ay isa sa kanila.

Isinilang noong 12 Enero 1849 sa Tarragona, Espanya, pumasok si Padre Sanchez sa seminaryo ng Tortosa sa edad na 13 at nang maglaon ay naging nobisyo ng orden ng mga Heswita. Nanumpa siya pagkalipas ng ilang taon, nang siya ay 18. Natatag ang kanyang pagmamahal sa panitikan sa Balaguer, Espanya at sa Avignon, Pransiya kung saan niya tinapos ang kanyang pag-aaral sa panitikan. Naging bihasa rin siya sa retorika, pilosopiya, at Latin.

Nagkrus ang landas nina Padre Sanchez at Rizal sa Ateneo Municipal de Manila. Kararating pa lamang niya sa Pilipinas noong 31 Oktubre 1872, nagturo sa paaralan, at naging guro ni Rizal mula 1874 hanggang 1875. Si Rizal, sa panahong ito, ay nasa ikaapat na taon na sa Ateneo Municipal.

Lubos na iginagalang ni Rizal si Padre Sanchez, na pinag-aralan niya ang matematika, retorika, Griyego, at Espanyol. Nang pumasok si Rizal sa kanyang klase, mababa pa ang Espanyol ng bata, ngunit mabilis siyang umunlad sa pagsasalita at paggamit ng wika sa tula. Inatasan ni Padre Sanchez ang batang “Pepito” na isalin sa taludtod ang dulang Italyanong St. Eustachius, Martyr, na nasusulat sa tuluyang Espanyol. Nakasulat ang pagmamahal ni Rizal sa kanyang guro sa panimula ng kanyang akda tungkol kay San Eustaquio, kung saan tinawag niya itong “aking pinakamamahal na propesor” at ipinahayag ang kanyang pasasalamat sa pagsisikap nitong tulungan siya sa kanyang pag-aaral.

Sinanay din niya pa si Rizal sa pagtula. Ang pagsasanay noon ay ang pagmumungkahi ng paksa, maging pangkasaysayan o panrelihiyon, at ang pagpapalawak ng mga tema sa pamamagitan ng mga tula. Isa pa sa kanyang mga atas kay Rizal ay ang pagsulat ng tula tungkol sa Calamba, ang bayang sinilangan nito.

Sa kabila ng papuri ni Rizal sa kanyang estilo ng pagtuturo, itinuring ng ibang mag-aaral si Padre Sanchez bilang mapag-alinlangan at mahiwaga. Nang maglaon ay bumalik si Padre Sanchez sa Europa, at naglagi sa Italya, Pransiya, at Espanya upang mag-aral. Inordenan siyang pari noong 1880, at bumalik sa Pilipinas bilang guro sa Ateneo Municipal noong 1881.

Sa paglipas ng mga taon, nanatiling magkaugnay sina Rizal at Padre Sanchez. Pinuri niya ang Noli Me Tangere ngunit binalaan din ang nobelista tungkol sa mga panganib dahil sa nilalaman ng nobela. Babalik si Padre Sanchez sa landas ng buhay ni Rizal nang irekomenda siya ni Padre Pastells na ipadala rin sa Dapitan sa panahon ng pagkatapon ni Rizal doon, “upang tingnan kung maaaring maibalik sa tamang landas ang naligaw na tupang ito”, tumutukoy sa mga pananaw ni Rizal laban sa klero. Pumasok din ang dalawa sa mga gawaing pang-agham sa Dapitan: paghahati ng kagamitang pang-agham, pagsasagawa ng mga paghuhukay na arkeolohiko, at paggawa ng relief map ng Mindanao. Umalis si Padre Sanchez sa Dapitan noong 1883 nang ilipat siya sa Tagana-an, Surigao. Nalampasan niya ng 32 taon ang buhay ng kanyang pinakamamahal na mag-aaral na si Rizal, at namatay sa sakit sa tiyan noong 21 Hulyo 1928.
bio.de:
Außer seiner Familie war es nur wenigen vergönnt, Dr. Rizals Genie in seiner Jugend und bis in sein Erwachsenenalter und sein Martyrium hinein zu erleben. Pater Francisco de Paula Sanchez, ein Jesuit, war einer von ihnen.

Geboren am 12. Januar 1849 in Tarragona, Spanien, trat Pater Sanchez mit 13 Jahren in das Seminar von Tortosa ein und wurde später Novize des Jesuitenordens. Nach einigen Jahren legte er mit 18 schließlich seine Gelübde ab. Seine Leidenschaft für die Literatur festigte sich in Balaguer in Spanien und in Avignon in Frankreich, wo er sein Literaturstudium abschloss. Auch in Rhetorik, Philosophie und Latein wurde er bewandert.

Pater Sanchez und Rizal kreuzten ihre Wege am Ateneo Municipal de Manila. Er war am 31. Oktober 1872 gerade auf den Philippinen angekommen, unterrichtete an der Schule und wurde von 1874 bis 1875 Rizals Lehrer. Rizal war zu dieser Zeit bereits im vierten Jahr am Ateneo Municipal.

Rizal schätzte Pater Sanchez außerordentlich; von dem Jesuiten lernte er Mathematik, Rhetorik, Griechisch und Spanisch. Als Rizal in seine Klasse eintrat, war sein Spanisch mäßig, doch er machte rasch Fortschritte im Sprechen und im dichterischen Gebrauch der Sprache. Pater Sanchez trug dem jungen „Pepito“ auf, das italienische Drama St. Eustachius, Martyr, in spanischer Prosa verfasst, in Verse zu übertragen. Rizals Zuneigung zu seinem Lehrer steht in der Einleitung seiner Arbeit über den heiligen Eustachius, wo er ihn „meinen geliebten Professor“ nannte und ihm für seine Bemühungen um seine Studien dankte.

Er bildete Rizal auch weiter in der Dichtkunst aus. Die Übung bestand damals darin, ein Thema vorzugeben, entweder historisch oder religiös, und die Motive in Gedichten zu entfalten. Eine weitere seiner Aufgaben für Rizal war, ein Gedicht über Calamba, dessen Heimatstadt, zu schreiben.

Trotz Rizals Lob seines Unterrichtsstils galt Pater Sanchez anderen Schülern als pessimistisch und rätselhaft. Später kehrte Pater Sanchez nach Europa zurück und verbrachte Studienzeiten in Italien, Frankreich und Spanien. 1880 wurde er zum Priester geweiht und kehrte 1881 als Lehrer am Ateneo Municipal auf die Philippinen zurück.

Über die Jahre blieben Rizal und Pater Sanchez in Verbindung. Er lobte den Noli Me Tangere, warnte den Romancier aber auch vor den Gefahren, die vom Inhalt des Buches ausgingen. Pater Sanchez kehrte in Rizals Lebensbahn zurück, als Pater Pastells empfahl, auch ihn während Rizals Verbannung nach Dapitan zu schicken, „um zu sehen, ob dieses verirrte Schaf auf den rechten Weg zurückgeführt werden kann“ — gemeint waren Rizals antiklerikale Ansichten. Die beiden wagten sich in Dapitan auch an wissenschaftliche Unternehmungen: Sie teilten wissenschaftliche Geräte, führten archäologische Ausgrabungen durch und fertigten eine Reliefkarte von Mindanao an. Pater Sanchez verließ Dapitan 1883, als er nach Tagana-an, Surigao, versetzt wurde. Er überlebte seinen geschätzten Schüler Rizal um 32 Jahre und starb am 21. Juli 1928 an einem Magenleiden.
